content.comment_body: Hello, I have installed a [product_name] with [product_name] communication module for a project where a daily SMS is sent to inform the owner about gas usage. I set up the [product_name] to obtain the time from an NTP server ([url]) since accurate timing is important for the application. This setup worked well until about a week ago when a red 'F' light appeared on the unit, and the SMS timestamps became inaccurate. Fortunately, the time in the [product_name] controller stayed correct. I initially suspected either the SIM card ran out of data or there was an NTP server issue. The SIM administrator confirmed there were no issues on their side. After testing diagnostics, mobile data is working, but NTP time synchronization is failing. I can still ping the NTP server from my laptop. 1 - Can anyone suggest a reliable, free NTP server in the UK? 2 - Should I suspect the NTP server or [product_name] as the problem? Both seem unlikely to fail, but given the ongoing SMS functionality and error messages, the server appears to be the issue. Thanks

Hello [user_name], Here are some points: + Is the latest firmware update installed on the communication module? What [product_name] controller is being used? (Order number, firmware version) Some [product_name] controllers have available firmware updates. The update applies only for modules ending in [article_no] with specific FS-stand numbers. If your controller runs [version_no], you should update the firmware. Another suggestion: try a different free NTP server and see if it resolves the issue. There are many listed on Google, and it isn't necessary to select a local NTP server. Hope this helps.

Hi [user_name], Thanks for your response. I currently have only the communication module for testing—the [product_name] controller remains on site. The module has firmware V2.1.5, and the controller is a recent model purchased in Nov 2018, but I can't check its firmware version remotely (perhaps I missed it in the configuration area). I switched the NTP server to time.google.com and it worked again; switching back to the previous server immediately caused it to fail, which suggests the issue is with the NTP server. I will leave it as time.google.com and once the controller is back on site, I’ll observe its operation and report updates. Looks like the NTP server was the root cause. Thanks again.

The firmware version can be read through the software: Tools > Transfer > Show FW version. If your controller was purchased in November 2018, it is likely a [product_name] model [version_no]. You can identify it by checking if the order number ends with [article_no]. The firmware version would likely be [version_no].

analysis.insight_summary: Users reported a loss of NTP time synchronization on the communication module, causing automated SMS reports to show incorrect timestamps, though SMS transmission itself remained unaffected. Troubleshooting concentrated on external NTP server reliability and firmware management for both the communication module and controller. Diagnostics revealed the failure was specific to the chosen NTP server, reinforcing the significance of dependable network services for applications requiring precise time synchronization.
analysis.user_expectations: User expects the system to reliably maintain time synchronization to ensure accurate SMS timestamps and dependable communication functionality.
